We provide inclusive education within a safe, nurturing environment where children’s needs are met.
Welcome to New Barn School
New Barn School provides highly effective education, therapy, welfare and support for both boys and girls aged from 6 to 19 years who have social, emotional and mental health needs (SEMH), as well as other complex needs.
New Barn School, across our three sites, delivers a structured programme of education, tailored to each student’s individual needs and considering their Education, Health and Care plans. Students are taught in small cohorts and individually, by fully qualified teachers and instructors.
New Barn school sites include:
Please see ‘our sites’ area for more information.
Willow Farm: Welford RG20 8HZ
Home Farm: Welford RG20 8HR
River View House: Newbury RG14 2PS
Testimonials
Two years ago, if you had asked me will E be in full time education, I would have said no. I am so impressed with what has been achieved for him.
We are really proud of one of our students who has been engaging consistently with our online learning provision. Their attendance and commitment have been excellent, and they have shown great determination with their studies. Recently, they have also come into school to sit their maths exams, which is a fantastic step and a real achievement. Well done CH for your hard work and perseverance.
Secondary Staff Member
I wanted to say thank you so much for having me in this week for the VR Workshop. It was an honor and absolute pleasure to work with the students. The work you all do at New Barn is amazing and the teachers and assistants are incredible.
Great progress at the moment. We have noticed how much happier he seems at home, I think this is the best he has been at/with school in a long time. Many thanks for your role in this.
I can’t thank you guys enough for what you have done. There’s a school that’s out there that can actually meet his needs and teach him what’s right from wrong.
I wanted to say how pleased I have been at how well R has settled into the secondary school. Special thanks must go to his music teacher, who has really bought out a talent in drumming, we had no idea was there! Thank you. Also his tutor, Emily for all of her hard work. The positive reports I get at the end of the week have been so nice to hear and a testament to the support he is receiving.
I just wanted to say that the carnival yesterday was great. You could see all the effort made by the team and children. I know these events take lots of planning and organising. Please send my thanks to all involved.
Our Vision
New Barn School differs from most schools as it can offer a bespoke curriculum for every student. Its ethos is based around nurturing, making progress and helping young people feel safe and cared for.
Our Values
The school places particular emphasis on collaboration.This way our students move on comfortably to engage with education and reach their full potential.
Our Aims
We believe that our pupils deserve the very best. Our school is passionate about the welfare and inclusion of all children and young people.
© OFG Education 2026

Parents & Carers
The parents and carers of the children and young people we educate and care for are so important, and we take care to give them all the expert ongoing support they need at every stage of their partnership with us.
From the moment they make their first enquiry and right through the child or young person’s time in one of our schools or residential homes, we’re there for them with tailored advice and support.
Tune in to Autism Unpacked, where we’re navigating SEN together through honest conversations, expert insight, lived experience and practical advice.
We’re joined by professionals from education and therapy, alongside parents, carers and people with lived experience, to share practical insights, explore the topics that matter and help families and those supporting children and young people feel better informed.

Home Our Approach Careers
Careers
Choosing which direction to take after leaving school is a big decision.
At New Barn School we aim to provide individualised education for our students to improve life outcomes. We recognise that supporting our students to find the right pathway for them is a large part of this. We are here to support our students and make sure they know all the options open to them.
We provide our students with meaningful career-related opportunities and activities throughout their time with us. Our Careers programme is designed to give our young people the skills, knowledge and confidence they require to find and access a career they will enjoy and thrive in.
By using the Gatsby Benchmarks and CDI framework as a guide, the Incredible Futures and NCFE Employability Skills programmes as sources we have a careers programme that meet the needs of all students. Alongside our dedicated careers lessons the students will also receive advice from an independent Level 6 Careers Advisor.
The Gatsby benchmarks are seen as best practice for careers guidance within schools. We use Gatsby benchmarks to measure our program and complete termly Compass evaluations. The Gatsby benchmarks are:
We have access to Careerpilot, which can be used as a source of information during Careers lessons. There is a parent zone on their website filled with lots of useful information, which can be found here: https://www.careerpilot.org.uk/parent-zone
Other useful websites include:
The National Careers Service: https://nationalcareers.service.gov.uk/
Talking Futures: https://www.talkingfutures.org.uk/
Amazing Apprenticeships: https://amazingapprenticeships.com/
The Careers Lead at New Barn School is Adele Griffiths. Please get in touch with any queries:
Adele.Griffiths@acornnewbarnschool.co.uk.

Referrals and admissions
New Barn School admits pupils from three of the residential homes in the Hampshire group, Acorn Cottage, Ramsworth and The Farmhouse as well as day pupils.
The registered age range for pupils is 6-19 years old and covers Key Stages 1, 2, 3, 4 & 5. Pupils are referred through the children’s homes from primarily social service departments from across England.
If you’d like to make a referral or you simply want to know more, please don’t hesitate to get in touch.
© OFG Education 2026

Home Our Approach Curriculum
Curriculum
New Barn School aims for students to be safe, happy and to engage positively in their learning and holistic development.
The school actively promotes a positive educational culture, through which students’ efforts are privately and publicly acknowledged to celebrate individual achievements and enhance their self-esteem. This creates an environment in which they want to achieve their best.
Qualifications are important but not the only purpose in which New Barn students can fulfil and achieve their full potential.
At New Barn, students aim to arrive at similar destinations as those in more formal educational settings. They just take a different route. The School provides every student with a broad, balanced, differentiated and relevant curriculum based on the National Curriculum guidelines. A comprehensive 14-16 curriculum Pathway is available at New Barn and at local colleges. This offers GCSE, BTEC, ASDAN, NVQ, DofE and other external examinations, catering for their current and future needs.
As students’ progress, they are helped to organize their own time and we guide them in developing their own sense of discipline and academic motivation. In secondary, students meet with their tutor twice daily. By providing structure and support, we encourage independence and responsibility to grow from an early age.
Life in Modern Britain
New Barn School aims to prepare pupils for life in modern Britain. We promote fundamental British Values through teaching about democracy, individual liberty and mutual respect and tolerance of those with different faiths and beliefs.
British values is taught in all aspects of the curriculum. New Barn School also has regular assemblies dedicated to British Values.
We urge students to follow their natural curiosity. They have a huge range of chances to engage with subjects that interest them, both in and outside the classroom. Accreditations are sought to produce a connection to academic enthusiasm and also the outside world.

Home Our Approach Clinical therapy
Clinical therapy
Our therapeutic model recognises that all the children and young people we support are individual and our provision is tailored to meet their needs and wishes from the point of admission and throughout their journey with us.
Therapeutic support within the school is led by the Clinical Lead, Georgia Bartlett, and is delivered by a core multidisciplinary team of clinicians made up of Psychology, Psychotherapy, Speech and Language Therapy and Occupational Therapy. The team are able to undertake a full range of specialist cognitive and mental wellbeing assessments which inform a child or young person’s individual clinical plan and if indicated, offer individual, group, direct and or indirect therapeutic interventions.
The school’s designated team reflects the needs of the children and young people that learn with us, however additional support can also be accessed from other specialists within the wider Clinical Team. This enables us to be responsive to any newly identified, time limited or changing needs of a child or young person throughout their placement with us.
Offering highly specialised screening, assessment, consultation, reflective practice supervision and bespoke training, the embedded Clinical Team work directly with the education team to develop a shared understanding of the child’s presenting needs and difficulties which may act as barriers to their personal and educational development as well as identify areas of strength which can support them to achieve, enjoy and fulfil their aims and wishes.
The clinical team support the education team in developing a pupil centred curriculum which proactively promotes the children and young people’s emotional, social and mental health. We aim to deliver the highest quality provision which maximises each person’s quality of life and personal achievements. All staff are trained in ‘Attachment Theory, ‘Child Development and Understanding Play’ and aspire to using PACE (Playful, Accepting, Curiosity and Empathetic). Our evidence informed models are based on best practice guidance and are governed through the OFG Education Governance Framework.
© OFG Education 2026

Home About Us Meet the team
Meet our team
Headteacher – Krishna Purbhoo
Amelia Lawrence
Business Manager
I joined New Barn School in 2023 and am proud to serve as the School Business Manager. My role is all about making sure the school’s operational side runs smoothly, from finance and compliance to health and safety, recruitment, and facilities management.
Before joining New Barn, I worked in a variety of administrative and operational roles, including managing electrical office operations and front-of-house services. These experiences helped me develop a practical, solution-focused approach and a passion for organisation and efficiency.
I enjoy finding ways to improve processes, supporting colleagues, and ensuring that staff have the resources they need to provide the best possible experience for our pupils. Being part of a team that makes a real difference to young people’s lives is one of the most rewarding aspects of my role.
Teresa Norris
Assistant Headteacher & DSL
I joined New Barn School in 2018 and have over 20 years’ experience in special education.
As Assistant Headteacher and Designated Safeguarding Lead, I play a key role in ensuring that every pupil at New Barn School feels safe, happy, and supported to be the very best version of themselves. I oversee safeguarding, attendance and well-being working closely with pupils, families, and professionals to provide a holistic and child-centred approach to support.
I am passionate about championing the needs of children and young people and believe that positive relationships are at the heart of successful outcomes. I work collaboratively with staff and families to help pupils overcome challenges, build confidence, and achieve their individual goals.
With a strong commitment to safeguarding and wellbeing, I strive to create an environment where every pupil feels understood, valued, and able to flourish.
Paul Clark
Facilities Manager
I have worked in site and facilities management within schools for a number of years, having held caretaker positions at a number of local primary schools. Throughout my career, I have developed extensive experience in maintaining safe, secure, and welcoming learning environments for pupils, staff, and visitors.
I enjoy the variety that comes with working in education, from overseeing site maintenance and health and safety compliance to supporting the day-to-day operations that help schools run effectively. I take pride in being organised, proactive, and ensuring that facilities are maintained to a high standard.
I enjoy being part of a school community and making a positive contribution behind the scenes to ensure pupils have the best possible environment in which to learn and thrive.
Fun Fact: I enjoy DIY projects, spending time watching football, and spending time with my grandchildren.
Rebekah Mann
Clinical Lead
Annabelle Lowe
Riverview Head of School
I am a dedicated and experienced school leader with over 18 years of experience in education across both the UK and international settings, specialising in inclusion, SEND and school improvement. I am currently the Head of School at River View House, here at New Barn School, and have worked here for almost a year to date.
My career has included a range of leadership roles, including Assistant Headteacher for Inclusion, Acting Deputy Headteacher, Deputy Headteacher and Head of Extended Learning Needs Programmes. Throughout my career, I have championed inclusive practice and worked to ensure that every child feels understood, valued and supported to reach their full potential. I firmly believe that education should focus not only on academic achievement, but also on developing confidence, resilience, independence and a sense of belonging.
I hold a Master’s Degree in Special Educational Needs and Inclusion (Distinction), the NASENCO qualification and the National Professional Qualification for Headship (NPQH). These qualifications, alongside extensive practical experience, underpin my commitment to providing high-quality, inclusive education and creating positive outcomes for children and young people with additional needs.
Fun Fact: When I’m not at school, I love spending time outdoors. Whether it’s hiking in the countryside, swimming in lakes, training for a running event or exploring new places, being outside helps me recharge and find inspiration for the week ahead.
Abi Davies
Riverview Deputy Head
I am the Deputy Headteacher at the Secondary site of New Barn School, with a particular focus on trauma-informed practice. Over the past year, I have helped build our whole-school, trauma-informed approach to behaviour from the ground up, and I lead on keeping every student, and the adults around them, feeling safe.
I hold a degree in Psychology and a Master’s in Transformational Leadership, which looked closely at how psychological theory translates into everyday practice with young people. I’m endlessly curious about what actually helps students with social, emotional and mental health needs thrive, both in the classroom and beyond.
I believe a calm mind learns best, and I try to bring the same calm to how I lead, even on the busiest days (and in a school like ours, there are plenty of those!).
Fun fact: I’m a keen hiker and runner. Ask me about the time I submitted Scafell Pike in under fours hours!
Eleanor Hickey
Riverview Assistant Headteacher
I am the Assistant Head at River View House, New Barn School. Throughout my career, I have been privileged to support children and young people from a wide range of backgrounds, each with their own unique strengths and needs. My experience spans both primary and secondary education across mainstream schools and alternative provisions both in England and overseas.
Most recently, I oversaw inclusion in a large school supporting pupils aged 3 to 19. This role provided me with experience of the diverse ways that individual needs can present at different stages of development, strengthening my understanding of how to provide effective, personalised support for every learner.
I have a particular passion for English and am an enthusiastic reader. In my teaching, I strive to inspire a lifelong love of reading, believing that anyone who says they do not enjoy reading simply has not found the right book yet.
I hold a Master’s degree in Education and am committed to lifelong learning, continually seeking opportunities to develop my knowledge and practice. One of the most rewarding aspects of my role is building positive relationships with students and their families, working together to ensure every young person feels supported, valued, and empowered to achieve their full potential.
Fun fact: When I adopted my dog from the Middle East, she was already called Elizabeth, named after Queen Elizabeth, because she would only respond to commands spoken with an English accent!
Liam Bampton
Willow Farm Head of School
Sue Carey
Willow Farm Deputy Head
Adele Allen
Willow Farm Assistant Headteacher
My career in education spans more than 20 years, beginning in outdoor education before moving into the classroom. This diverse experience has shaped my belief that every child learns differently and deserves opportunities to flourish both academically and personally. I have been part of the New Barn School community for the past three years, where I am proud to serve as an Assistant Headteacher.
I hold a BA (Hons) in Early Childhood Studies, a PGCE in Primary Education, and an NPQ in Leading Teaching. I am currently completing my NPQ for Senior Leadership (NPQSL). Throughout my career, I have been passionate about ensuring every child is recognised for their unique strengths and supported to achieve their full potential. I believe that with the right relationships, encouragement, and opportunities, every pupil can develop the confidence, skills, and independence they need to thrive. I am committed to maintaining high standards while creating a safe, nurturing environment where every pupil can thrive, celebrate their achievements, and develop the confidence to embrace new challenges. Seeing our pupils grow in confidence, overcome challenges, and achieve their own personal successes is the most rewarding part of my role.
Fun Fact: Outside of school, I love spending time outdoors and challenging myself with new adventures. I have climbed several mountains in the UK, and even skydived near the Great Barrier Reef. My dream is to climb Mount Everest!
Joanne Jones
Willow Farm Assistant Headteacher

Home About Us What we do
What We Do
At New Barn School we support students between the ages of 6 and 19 years of age who have a range of social, emotional and mental health needs. Our aim is very simple: we want to equip every child with the skills, knowledge and confidence that they need to be successful in their future.
Many children come to us with very complex needs, communication difficulties and associated challenging behaviour. We always look beyond the issues and potential barriers to learning and recognise the innate potential within. We invest time with each individual child to recognise and understand their learning needs so that we can put in place the right support package.
We pride ourselves on preparing our pupils for the next stage of their lives – not just academically but socially and emotionally and all of our pupils are encouraged to reach high standards in every aspect.
Our aim is simple, to provide outstanding care for children at New Barn, helping them to be the best they can be. We deliver a broad, balanced rich learning environment through the National Curriculum, educational and life skills, vocational opportunities as well as any additional support they need to achieve this. Built on trust and partnerships between pupils, parents and our wonderful team of teachers and support staff, you will see that our school has a lovely community atmosphere.
© OFG Education 2026
